QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_27

question.text: In the context of AIF 'secondaries' (secondary exit of an LP's unit capital / partnership interest), which statement is CORRECT?

answer.text: Secondaries are exchange-traded on NSE and BSE at daily NAV-based prices.
Unfunded commitments of the exiting investor CANNOT be transferred to the in-coming investor.
SEBI prohibits LP secondaries in all close-ended AIFs.
Secondaries typically occur at a negotiated price, often at a substantial discount to NAV, and usually require review of the contribution agreement for consents required.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 12: 'Secondary transactions take place at a negotiated price, often at a substantial discount to net asset value (NAV) ... the terms of the contribution agreement need to be examined to ascertain the possibility, consents required from other co-investors or the manager and associated issues. Usually, if there are outstanding commitments of the exiting investor, these are transferred to the in-coming investor along with the existing unit capital.' The Trap: Exchange-trading (Option A) describes listed securities, not illiquid private-market LP interests. Unfunded commitments ARE transferable (Option B is wrong). Blanket prohibition (Option C) is invented. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers secondaries. XXI-B PMS uses intra-day market transfers — very different. XIX-B Cat III may have more frequent liquidity windows, but not secondaries as defined here. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a 'secondaries playbook' into your fund docs: pre-agreed ROFR list (existing LPs), list of permitted transferees, and Manager consent criteria. This makes secondaries executable without renegotiation.
